articles.blogTitle: China Supplier Verification Checklist for Nigerian Importers
articles.blogContent:
A Chinese supplier can be real and still be wrong for your order. That is the first thing Nigerian importers must understand. Verification is not only about avoiding obvious scams. It is about confirming that the supplier can actually produce, pack, document and deliver the product you need at the quality level your market or business requires.

This checklist is a supporting guide to how to find a reliable supplier in China from Nigeria. Use it before you pay a supplier, before you approve samples, and before you scale repeat orders. If the order is for a company, school, NGO, office rollout or resale business, do not treat supplier verification as optional. Use Corporate Sourcing when the risk justifies proper sourcing support.

Checking a Chinese supplier for a UK-bound order

The checks below are written for Nigerian importers. For a UK order, keep the same evidence-first approach but make your destination and intended use explicit. Our guide to importing from China to the UK explains the available buying routes.

Separate three questions in your supplier file: is this the business you think you are dealing with, can it make your exact product, and what evidence supports selling that product in your target market? A business registration document answers a different question from a sample or a product test report.

  • Identity: record the supplier's legal name, address, invoice issuer and payment beneficiary. Ask for an explanation of mismatches and verify changes through an established contact before acting on new payment instructions.
  • Capability: request evidence for your model, material and production quantity. A catalogue containing a similar item is not confirmation that the factory can make your version.
  • Documents: check that any supplied report identifies the actual product or model being quoted. A file labelled certificate is not enough information to approve the order.
  • Order control: record approved specifications, sample references, inspection expectations and how substitutions or defects will be handled.

Use the official UK product safety guidance to identify the next checks for your category. Supplier verification reduces uncertainty; it is not a guarantee of every unit's quality or a blanket compliance approval.

1. Confirm what the supplier actually sells

Many suppliers show broad catalogues, but serious importers look for specialization. A seller who lists phone cases, blenders, shoes, solar panels and handbags may be a trading seller, not a focused manufacturer. That is not automatically bad, but you must know what you are dealing with. Ask whether the supplier manufactures the product, trades it, or sources it from another factory.

Check the store's product history on platforms such as 1688, Alibaba or Taobao. Look at how many related products they sell, how consistent the listings are, how long the store has been active, and whether the product photos look like one stable line or random uploads from different sources.

2. Check response quality, not just response speed

Fast replies are useful, but quality of reply matters more. A reliable supplier should answer specific questions directly. If you ask for material, carton size, warranty, plug type, battery health, grade, certification, lead time or packaging, the answer should not be vague. Vague answers before payment usually become expensive arguments after delivery.

For technical products, ask the same question in two ways and see whether the answer stays consistent. For laptops, ask about processor generation, RAM, storage type, screen size, battery condition and keyboard layout. For phones, ask about model, network, storage, grade, battery health and accessories. Read how to import phones from China to Nigeria safely and how to import laptops from China to Nigeria safely before buying gadgets.

3. Request proof that matches your order

Do not ask for generic proof. Ask for proof related to your exact purchase. If you need black 500ml branded bottles, ask for real photos or videos of that item, not a catalogue cover. If you need a machine, request a test-run video with your expected material or a closely related material. If you need laptops, request photos or videos showing the exact grade and configuration.

Proof should help you answer practical questions: does the product match the specification, can it be packed safely, is the quantity available, and does the supplier understand the final use? If the order is custom, a sample is often cheaper than correcting a full shipment later.

4. Verify price realism

A low price is not proof of a good deal. Compare three or more suppliers where possible. If one quote is far below the others, ask what is excluded. It may be a different material, smaller size, lower grade, no packaging, no accessory, weaker warranty or a different model. Cheap listings often hide differences in variant details.

Before paying, estimate the real landed cost with the Landed Cost Estimator. If you ignore shipping, duty, clearing and local delivery, you may think the supplier is cheap while the final Nigerian cost is not viable. Read how to calculate landed cost before importing from China to Nigeria for the full method.

5. Confirm payment and delivery structure

Supplier payment should follow confidence, not emotion. Confirm RMB amount, invoice, beneficiary details, production or dispatch timeline, China local delivery cost, and what happens if the supplier cannot fulfil the exact specification. If you already trust the supplier and only need RMB payment, sign in and use Pay Supplier. If trust is still uncertain, do not rush payment.

When goods are ready, confirm internal China tracking, warehouse address, carton count, gross weight and carton dimensions. If you need logistics after purchase, use Ship With Us and compare shipping assumptions with the shipping and landed cost pillar.

6. Use a written verification file

  • Supplier name, platform link and contact details.
  • Exact product specification and variants.
  • Quote, payment terms and RMB amount.
  • Photos, videos, sample result or inspection evidence.
  • Carton dimensions, gross weight and quantity.
  • Compliance notes for Customs, SON or NAFDAC where relevant.
  • Final landed cost and selling price assumption.

Turn the checks into a supplier decision

Keep one file for each supplier and product. Put the company's legal name, trading name, address, contact person and payment beneficiary on the first page. Copy the exact product specification and quantity from the quotation. If the licence, invoice and bank instructions use different names, ask for a written explanation and supporting documents before paying. A plausible explanation is a reason to investigate, not proof by itself.

For a factory claim, request evidence tied to the actual goods and production site. A business licence shows that a company exists; it does not prove that it makes the item in your quotation. Ask for a live demonstration of the specified model or a sample that can be tested independently. When a trading company is involved, record who will be accountable for defects and which entity will appear on export paperwork.

Record how each claim was checked. A dated video call, sample inspection, document comparison and reference from an identifiable buyer are different kinds of evidence. Save the original documents and the questions you asked, not only a screenshot of a marketplace badge. If a document cannot be checked, mark that point unresolved rather than treating a polished PDF as verification.

Write the acceptance conditions before authorising production: approved sample, agreed materials, dimensions and tolerances, packaging, inspection method, delivery term and remedy for nonconforming goods. Tie a later payment milestone to evidence you can actually inspect. If an intermediary will inspect, give them the same version of the specification that the supplier received.

A supplier decision can be recorded as approved, conditional or declined. Conditional approval should name the missing proof and the person responsible for obtaining it. This makes it possible to compare two suppliers on evidence rather than the speed of their replies. Recheck the file when the product, beneficiary or shipping arrangement changes; yesterday's approval does not automatically cover a different order.

Use the landed cost estimator once the quotation is specific enough to compare. If you need help checking a supplier or arranging an inspection, describe the product and unresolved points through corporate sourcing. For the broader buying sequence, read the China import guide. Supplier verification should leave you with a decision file that another person in your business can understand and challenge.

articles.blogTitle: How Nigerian Importers Should Pay Chinese Suppliers in RMB Without Losing Control
articles.blogContent:
Paying a Chinese supplier is not just a transaction. It is the point where your import plan becomes real risk. Before payment, you can still compare suppliers, correct specifications, cancel a weak deal or ask for samples. After payment, your leverage depends on the supplier's honesty, the platform rules, the payment structure and the records you kept.

This guide explains how Nigerian importers should approach RMB payments with control. It supports the earlier article on how to pay Chinese suppliers from Nigeria safely and connects directly to the signed-in Pay Supplier service on Sure Imports. The aim is simple: pay only when the commercial structure is clear enough to defend.

Payment should come after supplier clarity

Do not pay because a supplier is pressuring you. Pay because the order is clear. Before sending money, confirm the exact product, variant, quantity, unit price, local China delivery, packaging, lead time, refund or replacement position, and what evidence the supplier will provide before dispatch. If the supplier cannot answer these points clearly, payment is premature.

For marketplace purchases from 1688, Alibaba, Taobao or Pinduoduo, variant clarity matters. A link can contain multiple colours, sizes, grades and bundles. Make sure the supplier or buyer knows the exact option you are paying for.

Understand when RMB payment makes sense

RMB payment is useful when you are dealing with a Chinese supplier who prices in yuan or when the best supply route is on a domestic Chinese platform. Many strong prices on 1688 and similar platforms are RMB-based. The buyer in Nigeria must then solve payment, communication, China local delivery and shipping.

Use Pay Supplier when you already have a supplier and need to pay in RMB through your Sure Imports account. Use Buy From Chinese Websites when you have product links and want Sure Imports to process the website purchase. Use Corporate Sourcing when the supplier itself still needs to be found or verified.

Keep payment records like a business

Every payment should have a file. Save supplier name, platform link, invoice, agreed specification, amount in RMB, exchange rate used, naira equivalent, payment reference, date, and the person who approved the payment. If you are buying for a company, this is not bureaucracy. It protects finance, procurement and the business owner.

A payment without a specification is weak evidence. A supplier can later say a cheaper grade was ordered, a different variant was selected, or packaging was not included. Screenshots and written confirmation reduce that risk. Keep them before funds move.

Split payments when the order requires it

For some orders, especially custom, machine, high-value or corporate orders, full upfront payment may not be the best structure. Depending on supplier terms, you may need deposit, sample approval, production balance or inspection before release. The right structure depends on product category, supplier history and order size.

If the supplier insists on full payment for a serious order without enough proof, slow down. Ask whether samples, staged payment or third-party inspection are possible. For machinery and technical products, read existing Sure Imports guides on machine sourcing and factory test runs before approving payment.

Do not separate payment from landed cost

Many Nigerian importers ask whether they can afford the supplier payment but ignore whether they can afford the full order. Supplier payment is only one part of landed cost. Add China local delivery, procurement fees, shipping, duty, clearing, local delivery and exchange buffer. Use the Landed Cost Estimator before payment and read Nigeria Customs duty on goods from China.

If you are buying bulky goods, also check CBM with the CBM Calculator. A product can be cheap in RMB and expensive to ship. The correct decision is not always to pay the cheapest supplier. The correct decision is to buy the product that lands in Nigeria at a profitable and defensible cost.

A simple RMB payment checklist

  • Supplier identity and platform link confirmed.
  • Product specification, variant and quantity written down.
  • RMB amount, exchange rate and naira equivalent recorded.
  • China local delivery and dispatch timeline confirmed.
  • Photos, video, sample or inspection plan agreed where needed.
  • Shipping method and landed cost estimated before payment.
  • Payment submitted through a trackable process in your Sure Imports account.

Make an RMB payment traceable from invoice to receipt

Start with a pro forma invoice that names the legal seller, the exact goods, quantity, currency, payment schedule and receiving account. Compare its beneficiary with the supplier identity you verified. A last-minute instruction to pay a different individual or account is a material change: pause and confirm it through a separate, previously established contact channel. Keep the original invoice and the revised instruction so the change is visible.

Agree what the RMB amount covers. Product price, domestic delivery in China, export handling, international freight and Nigerian charges may sit with different parties. Mark each line as included, excluded or still to be quoted. A favourable exchange rate cannot rescue an order whose freight, duty or quality costs have not been estimated. Keep the quote currency and any conversion used in your buying file.

If the order allows staged payment, define the event that releases each stage. A deposit may start production; a later amount should be linked to the agreed evidence, such as a passed inspection or shipping documents. Specify who approves that evidence and how a dispute is raised. Splitting transfers without a written milestone does not create control over the goods.

Before each transfer, confirm the beneficiary, amount, reference and invoice version. Save the payment instruction, transaction confirmation, date and any fees in the same file. Ask the supplier to acknowledge receipt against the invoice and update the remaining balance. If an intermediary handles RMB payment, request a clear record connecting your Naira payment, the conversion and the supplier's RMB receipt.

After payment, reconcile what was ordered with what is being made or packed. A receipt establishes that money moved; it does not establish product conformity. Compare the supplier's final packing list and inspection evidence with the invoice before treating the order as ready for international shipment. Record any change to quantity, specification or delivery date and its effect on the remaining balance.

The landed cost estimator can help you test whether the full order remains viable. If the payment is part of a wider procurement job, corporate sourcing can coordinate the supplier and inspection work. Existing account holders can use the Pay Supplier flow for a documented payment request. The practical goal is an auditable chain from quote to beneficiary, transfer, supplier receipt and delivered goods.

articles.blogTitle: Best Chinese Wholesale Websites for Nigerian Importers and When To Use Each One
articles.blogContent:
The best Chinese wholesale website for a Nigerian importer depends on what you are buying, how much support you need, whether the order is simple or technical, and whether you are buying for resale or for a business. There is no single best platform for every situation. 1688 can be excellent for domestic China wholesale pricing. Alibaba can be better for export-facing supplier conversations. Taobao can help with trend discovery. DHGate can work for smaller international buys. Pinduoduo can reveal aggressive consumer pricing, but needs caution.

This guide supports the pillar on how to buy from Chinese websites in Nigeria. Use it when you are deciding where to search first. If you already have product links, use Buy From Chinese Websites. If you need the right supplier found rather than a link processed, use Corporate Sourcing.

1688: strong for wholesale pricing and resale stock

1688 is often the strongest starting point for Nigerian importers looking for wholesale pricing. Many products listed there are meant for the Chinese domestic market, which can make prices attractive. The challenge is that the platform is not designed around Nigerian buyers. Communication, RMB payment, China local delivery, variants and supplier verification must be handled properly.

Use 1688 for resale products, accessories, household items, packaging, simple electronics, fashion items and items where you can compare many sellers. Do not use it blindly for technical products or high-risk categories without verification. For safety, use the Sure Imports link submission flow when you have links, or request sourcing support when the order is complex.

Alibaba: better for export conversations and business procurement

Alibaba is often better for custom orders, factory conversations, export documentation, samples, branded packaging and higher quantity negotiations. Prices may not always look as low as 1688, but the supplier conversation can be more suitable for corporate buyers.

Use Alibaba when you need specifications, production timelines, samples, branding or supplier documentation. But do not assume Alibaba automatically removes risk. Verify supplier specialization, compare quotes, request videos and understand payment terms. The article on how to find a reliable supplier in China from Nigeria gives a broader verification method.

Taobao: useful for consumer products and product discovery

Taobao is useful for spotting consumer trends, styles, small accessories and products that may not yet be obvious on wholesale platforms. Nigerian importers can use it for samples and idea discovery, but should be careful when scaling because retail sellers may not support bulk, stable supply or proper packaging.

If a Taobao product performs well, the next step is to find a stable supply source. That may mean searching 1688, asking Sure Imports to source the product, or finding a supplier who can handle repeat orders. Discovery is not the same as procurement.

Pinduoduo and DHGate: opportunity with limits

Pinduoduo can show aggressive pricing on consumer items, but quality and seller reliability can vary. DHGate can work for smaller international purchases, but Nigerian importers still need to compare total cost. Shipping, platform assumptions and product grade can change the real economics.

Use these platforms with a clear checklist. Ask what is included, what grade is supplied, what packaging is used, and whether the product can be repeated. If the platform is only giving you a one-time cheap buy, it may not be enough to build a serious import business.

Match the platform to the buying goal

  • Use 1688 for wholesale price discovery and many resale products.
  • Use Alibaba for supplier conversations, custom orders and business procurement.
  • Use Taobao for trends, samples and consumer product ideas.
  • Use Pinduoduo cautiously for deal discovery and price comparison.
  • Use DHGate for smaller international purchases where the final cost still makes sense.
  • Use Sure Imports when you need Nigerian-facing payment, procurement, shipping and tracking support.

Do not choose a platform before calculating landed cost

A product that looks cheapest on one platform may not be cheapest when it lands in Nigeria. Add local China delivery, procurement support, shipping, Customs duty, clearing and local delivery. Use the Landed Cost Estimator and the Air vs Sea Calculator before making a final choice.

Choose a platform for the order you actually have

Start with the product and buying stage. A one-unit discovery purchase, a repeat wholesale order and a private-label production run need different levels of supplier discussion. Record the exact model, material, quantity, destination and acceptable delivery date before comparing listings. Otherwise a low displayed unit price can hide a different specification, minimum quantity or shipping arrangement.

Use 1688 to research Chinese domestic wholesale offers, but expect to verify the seller, payment route and delivery inside China. Alibaba can be a useful starting point when you need export-oriented quotations and written negotiation. Taobao is often more useful for observing consumer variants or testing a small purchase than for assuming a stable bulk supply line. Pinduoduo and DHGate may surface attractive offers; the listing price alone says little about repeat availability or a consistent batch.

Compare like with like. Save the product link and a screenshot of the chosen variant, then build a table with specification, quantity, unit price, domestic freight, packaging, supplier identity and return or defect terms. Ask whether the displayed price applies to your quantity. Two offers with the same photograph may have different materials, warranties or included accessories. Request a sample when the difference matters to the buyer.

Work out how the goods leave the platform. Confirm where the seller will send them, who receives and inspects them in China, what documents accompany the package and who resolves a discrepancy. A platform's buyer-protection rules may depend on the payment method and transaction terms; do not assume that an off-platform transfer has the same protection as an eligible platform order.

For a repeat order, keep a record of the actual received item, defects, packaging measurements and landed cost. Reopen the supplier comparison if the listing changes, stock disappears or the next batch differs from the sample. The best platform is the one that lets you buy the specified goods through a workable payment, inspection and delivery process at a viable total cost.

For a practical comparison of checkout routes, use the Chinese websites buying guide. If you already have product links, the Buy From Chinese Websites service can help organise a purchase. For a custom or repeat business specification, start with corporate sourcing and bring your comparison table rather than only a product image.

articles.blogTitle: Bulk Laptop Sourcing From China for Nigerian Businesses: What To Specify Before You Pay
articles.blogContent:
Bulk laptop sourcing is one of the easiest procurement categories to get wrong. Two laptops can have the same brand name and look similar in photos, yet differ in processor generation, RAM, storage type, battery condition, screen quality, keyboard layout, grade and real business usefulness. For Nigerian companies, schools, training centres, NGOs and teams, the cost of wrong specification is not only financial. It affects productivity.

This guide supports how to import laptops from China to Nigeria safely and the page for laptops for businesses. If you need a managed procurement route for company laptops, do not treat it as a casual website order. Use Corporate Sourcing or the dedicated business laptop page so the requirement is specified properly.

Define the real use case first

A laptop for data entry is not the same as a laptop for design, software development, video editing, accounting, call centre work or AI training. Before asking for prices, define what the laptops must do. List the applications, expected workload, user type, mobility needs, battery expectations and whether the devices will be used in one office or distributed across locations.

This prevents false savings. A cheaper machine that cannot run the required tools is not cheaper. It becomes downtime, complaints, replacement cost and procurement embarrassment. Start from function, then match specifications.

Specify processor generation, not only Core i5 or Core i7

Many buyers ask for Core i5 or Core i7 without stating generation. That is a serious mistake. A newer Core i5 can outperform an older Core i7. Ask for processor model and generation. Also specify minimum RAM, storage size, whether storage is SSD or HDD, screen size, resolution expectation and whether upgrade options matter.

For business use, SSD storage is usually important because it affects speed. RAM should match workload. If staff will use browsers, spreadsheets, video calls and business applications at the same time, underpowered machines will slow the team down.

Understand grade and condition language

If buying used, refurbished or open-box laptops, grade language matters. Grade A, B or C can mean different things depending on supplier. Ask what each grade allows: scratches, dents, screen marks, keyboard wear, battery health, charger condition and warranty position. Do not accept grade language without examples.

Request real photos or videos of sample units, not only catalogue photos. If possible, request a sample or inspection evidence before bulk release. For large orders, a small inspection cost can prevent a large procurement mistake.

Battery, keyboard and charger details are not minor

Battery condition affects user experience immediately. Keyboard layout affects usability. Charger quality affects safety and reliability. Nigerian businesses should specify acceptable battery health or backup expectation, keyboard preference and charger condition. If replacement chargers are included, ask whether they are original, compatible or third-party.

For teams, standardization matters. A mixed batch with inconsistent chargers, keyboards and battery performance can create support issues. It may still be acceptable if priced correctly, but it should be a deliberate decision, not a surprise.

Calculate total cost per usable device

Do not judge only supplier price per laptop. Calculate total cost per usable device after shipping, duty, clearing, local delivery, possible repairs and expected replacement rate. Use the Landed Cost Estimator and compare shipping with the Air vs Sea Calculator.

If the order is urgent for onboarding, training or project launch, timing may be more important than the lowest freight option. Read China to Nigeria shipping, Customs and landed cost before choosing logistics.

A procurement checklist for business laptops

  • Use case and required applications documented.
  • Processor model and generation specified.
  • Minimum RAM, SSD size and screen size agreed.
  • Grade, battery, keyboard and charger condition clarified.
  • Sample, photos, video or inspection evidence requested.
  • Landed cost per usable device calculated.
  • Procurement record saved in your Sure Imports account.

Approve a batch specification, not a laptop description

Build a line-item specification before asking for a bulk quote. Include manufacturer and model family, processor generation and exact processor, memory, storage type and capacity, screen size and resolution, ports, wireless hardware and operating-system requirements. Write any permitted substitutions beside the original item. “Core i5, 8 GB RAM” spans machines with materially different age and usefulness.

Set a measurable condition standard. For used or refurbished machines, agree how cosmetic grades are defined, which faults are excluded and what battery-health evidence will be supplied. Specify the keyboard layout, charger wattage, plug arrangement and whether a working original or compatible charger is included. Ask how each device will be labelled so a failed unit can be traced back to its batch and seller.

Test a sample against the tasks employees actually perform, including calls, browser-based tools and any specialist software. A successful boot is only the first check. Confirm the ports, camera, keyboard, screen, wireless connection, storage health and battery behaviour. If the sample passes, keep its recorded specification as the reference for the shipment inspection.

For inspection, agree a sampling plan and rejection rule before the goods are packed. Define which defects require replacement, repair, credit or rejection of the batch. Record serial numbers or other identifiers where available. A photograph of sealed cartons cannot show whether the machines inside match the processor, battery and charger terms you approved.

Calculate cost per usable laptop rather than only cost per unit shipped. Include freight, clearing, local delivery, expected replacements and setup work, using your own measured failure allowance where possible. A lower price can be false economy if the team loses working days replacing chargers, batteries or unusable devices. Put acceptance and after-sales responsibilities in the purchase order.

The landed cost estimator can help structure the cost comparison. For a specified corporate batch, corporate sourcing is the appropriate route to discuss samples, inspection and delivery. The laptop import guide covers the wider import steps; your batch sheet should remain the document that determines what can be accepted.

articles.blogTitle: How Nigerian Wholesalers Can Build Repeat Supply Lines From China
articles.blogContent:
A wholesaler does not win by importing once. A wholesaler wins by building repeat supply. The first order proves that a product can move. The second and third orders prove whether the supplier, packaging, landed cost, shipping route and customer demand can become a system. Nigerian wholesalers who treat every order as a fresh gamble will struggle to compound their advantage.

This guide is for retailers, market sellers, online vendors, distributors and business owners who want a stronger China to Nigeria supply system. It connects to the pillar on importing from China to Nigeria and the product research guide on profitable mini importation products in Nigeria.

Separate product testing from supply building

The first order should answer whether the product can sell. Keep it controlled. Do not overbuy because the supplier price looks attractive. Test demand, customer feedback, delivery speed, defect rate, packaging and actual profit. If the first order works, the second order should improve the system rather than merely repeat it.

Supply building starts when you document what worked. Which supplier delivered? Which variant sold fastest? Which colour was slow? What was the final landed cost? What complaints came from customers? What shipping method protected margin? Without this data, the next order is just another guess.

Build a preferred supplier file

Your supplier file should include supplier name, platform link, contact, product links, quote history, payment terms, carton data, defect notes and repeat-order performance. If the supplier improves over time, keep them close. If quality declines, record it and compare alternatives before the next payment.

For supplier selection, use how to find a reliable supplier in China from Nigeria and the supplier verification checklist. If the product becomes important to your business, consider Corporate Sourcing to find stronger supply options or negotiate better structure.

Standardize specifications

Repeat orders fail when specifications are loose. If customers liked a specific size, colour, material, grade or packaging, write it down. The supplier should not choose for you on the next order. Standardization also helps staff, partners or procurement agents buy correctly when you are not personally handling every detail.

For products with variants, create your own SKU names. This makes inventory and reorder decisions easier. A supplier's product title may change, but your internal SKU should remain stable.

Use landed cost history to protect margin

Margins change because exchange rates, shipping rates, duty assumptions and supplier prices change. Keep landed cost history for each order. Use the Landed Cost Estimator every time, not only on the first order. Use the Retail Price Builder when naira costs shift.

If a product's margin is shrinking, do not ignore it. You may need to increase price, change quantity, improve packaging, switch supplier, move from air to sea, or stop importing that product. Good wholesalers are disciplined about numbers.

Use shipping strategy as a competitive advantage

Many wholesalers choose shipping by habit. Better wholesalers compare route, speed, volume and cash flow. Air freight may help you restock fast and protect sales momentum. Sea freight may help you reduce cost on bulky repeat goods. Use the Air vs Sea Calculator and read China to Nigeria shipping, Customs and landed cost.

For goods already with suppliers, use Ship With Us. But make sure your supplier sends accurate carton data and tracking details. A messy supplier handover slows everything down.

Turn repeat supply into business assets

A reliable supplier list, landed cost history, product performance record and reorder system are business assets. They make your business more predictable. They also make it easier to hire help, raise working capital, plan stock and negotiate with customers.

If you are moving from small importation to wholesale or corporate supply, create a free Sure Imports account and keep your buying, supplier payment and shipping activity organized. The goal is not only to import. The goal is to build a supply machine that can survive pressure.

Repeat supply checklist

  • Test product demand before scaling quantity.
  • Save supplier and product records after every order.
  • Standardize SKUs, variants and specifications.
  • Track landed cost history and margin movement.
  • Compare air and sea based on cash flow and volume.
  • Use sourcing support when a product becomes strategic.
  • Keep all order evidence in one business file.

Manage the second order as carefully as the first

A successful test shipment is the beginning of a supply record, not proof that every later batch will be identical. Record the exact product specification, packaging, approved sample, supplier contact, delivery term, landed cost and defect findings from the first order. Give the specification a version number. When you reorder, the supplier should confirm that version or identify each proposed change in writing.

Set a reorder trigger based on sales and lead time. Note how many units sell in a typical period, how long production and shipping took on actual orders, and how much stock you need while the next shipment is in transit. Keep a reserve for delays without treating every slow-moving variant as essential stock. The trigger should be reviewed when demand or shipping conditions change.

Track landed cost by SKU and batch. Include domestic movement in China, freight, clearing, local delivery and damaged or rejected units. Compare the new quotation with the last paid order, not only with a marketplace price. If the supplier changes the minimum quantity, carton size or payment schedule, recalculate the cash tied up and the selling margin before approving the reorder.

Use a short incoming-goods check each time. Compare the received quantity, materials, colour, dimensions, labels and packaging with the approved version. Photograph deviations and record the supplier's remedy. A repeated supplier relationship should make discrepancies easier to resolve because both sides have a clear reference, not because the buyer stops inspecting.

Keep an alternative supplier or product plan for critical stock, but do not call two listings interchangeable until their specifications and samples have been compared. If the primary supplier cannot meet the schedule, decide whether the substitute is acceptable to your customers and what extra cost it creates. Record the decision so the next buyer does not unknowingly repeat a failed substitution.

Review the supply line after every completed shipment: time from purchase order to receipt, units accepted, final landed cost, sales speed and customer complaints. Use those facts to refine the next order. The shipping and landed-cost guide explains the wider cost structure; corporate sourcing can help when repeat specifications and supplier coordination need more formal control. A reliable supply line is a sequence of documented, checked orders.
